title: A Statistical Framework for Training Data Auditing of Large Language Models
abstract: arXiv:2611.26264v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Training-data auditing asks whether data of interest were used to train a large language model (LLM), a question central to privacy auditing, copyright protection, and benchmark-contamination detection. These concerns are particularly relevant to the use of copyrighted books and scientific papers in pre-training, as well as synthetic text and medical question-answer records in fine-tuning. In practice, training membership signals may be concentrated in only a few passages of a long document, making it important to aggregate evidence within each document without diluting these localized signals. Beyond individual documents, auditing a target collection requires an overall assessment based on the document-level evidence. In this paper, we propose a unified statistical framework for document-level membership inference, target-collection global auditing, and suspicious-subset identification. translated_title: 大语言模型训练数据审计的统计框架
translated_abstract: 训练数据审计旨在判断感兴趣的数据是否被用于训练大语言模型（LLM），这一问题对于隐私审计、版权保护和基准污染检测至关重要。这些问题在预训练中使用受版权保护的书籍和科学论文，以及在微调中使用合成文本和医疗问答记录时尤为突出。在实践中，训练成员信号可能仅集中在长文档的少数段落中，因此在每个文档内聚合证据而不稀释这些局部信号至关重要。除了单个文档之外，审计目标数据集还需要基于文档级证据进行整体评估。在本文中，我们提出了一个统一的统计框架，用于文档级成员推断、目标数据集全局审计以及可疑子集识别。我们整合了互补的块级成员信号（摘要在此处被截断）
tldr: 本文提出了一个统一的统计框架，用于大语言模型训练数据审计，涵盖文档级成员推断、目标数据集全局审计和可疑子集识别，能够有效聚合文档内局部成员信号并进行整体评估。
en_tdlr: This paper proposes a unified statistical framework for training data auditing of large language models, enabling document-level membership inference, target-collection global auditing, and suspicious-subset identification by aggregating localized membership signals without dilution.
